title: my_uncle_streamed_my_world
display_title: My Uncle Sold Access to My Minecraft World Behind My Back
share_line: Send this to whoever's family member monetized something that wasn't theirs.
beats: My uncle (41M) found out my private parkour world had a waitlist of 200 people, and he started selling invites for $15 each without asking me.
I only found out because a stranger messaged me asking why the seed he 'bought' didn't work.
Turns out my uncle had been screen-recording my world, claiming he built it, and running a whole Discord selling 'exclusive access.'
So I patched every course overnight, added a plate that triggered a fake corruption screen, then a message: 'This world belongs to someone your uncle stole from.'
He messaged me an hour later asking why forty people were refunding him and calling him a scammer in the family group chat.
Was I wrong to let his own customers expose him?
